CityHealth will provide two weeks of de-identified clinical notes; Redwood will run a benchmark harness (golden prompts + regression tests) to measure hallucination rate, format compliance, and P95 latency. Agreed metrics and timeline for pilot kickoff and follow-up.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (CityHealth CMO), Liam O'Connor (Head of Data), Sara Mitchell (Compliance)
Meeting ID: ff-cityhealth-20261203-001

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, i'm Jordan, AE on the account, and with me is Maya, our SE who will run the benchmark and the quality eval. Um, Aisha, Liam, Sara, thanks for joining.

[00:18] Aisha: Hi, all. Appreciate it. We wanted to make sure we nail success criteria up front - timeline is tight, Q1 pilot run ideally.

[00:30] Maya: Great. Today i'd like to scope workload sizing, agree on golden prompts and regression tests, and outline hallucination/format checks and scoring. We'll also confirm data delivery and timelines.

[00:45] Liam: Quick context — current stack is a mix, we have an internal inference cluster for some models but it's flaky for production. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated - security is a must, plus P95 latency under 600ms for conversational summarization.

[01:05] Sara: On compliance: SOC2 and HIPAA considerations. We'll need KMS integration and audit logs. Also data residency — notes need to live in our region.

[01:22] Jordan: Noted. Redwood supports KMS and VPC/private deployment options; we'll include SOC2 summary and a region mapping. For the POC, if you want hosted, we can still demonstrate a restricted dataset flow, otherwise Dedicated or Private is an option.

[01:40] Aisha: Success criteria from product side: accuracy of summaries (we'd like >85% clinical correctness on the golden set), hallucination rate under 1% on targeted prompts, format compliance (structured JSON output) 99% of the time, and P95 latency <600ms. Cost targets are secondary but still relevant.

[02:05] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll operationalize that into measurable metrics: exact-match / token-level F1 for structured fields, hallucination measured as non-evidenced assertions per 100 responses, and a format-validate pass rate. We'll also measure P50/P95/P99 latency and tokens per second.

[02:30] Liam: Workload sizing — expected production throughput if pilot goes well: about 1.2M requests per month, average request ~750 tokens in and 200 tokens out, with daily peaks around 120 RPS for short bursts. For the POC run, we can start with a scaled-down replay of 48k requests over a week to validate.

[02:55] Jordan: Good — for benchmarking we'll run both per-request latency and batched throughput tests. We'll need sample distribution: 70% summarization, 20% triage classification, 10% complex Q&A.

[03:15] Maya: Golden prompts — recommended approach: curate 150-200 high-value prompts across those buckets. CityHealth should nominate 50 seed golden prompts (critical cases) and Redwood will augment with 100 synthesized variants to stress edge cases. The golden set will be the canonical pass/fail for regression tests.

[03:40] Aisha: We'll pick the 50. Important they include examples that trigger hallucination risk — rare conditions, medication name collisions, and ambiguous patient history.

[03:55] Maya: Regression tests — we'll version the golden set and run nightly gated comparisons during the POC. Any model update or config change that causes >2% degradation on primary metrics triggers rollback. We'll store results in a simple dashboard and attach diffs for flagged prompts.

[04:18] Sara: On hallucination checks, how do you detect non-evidenced assertions? Machine heuristics often miss subtle errors.

[04:28] Maya: Good point. We'll use a hybrid approach: automated evidence-matching for explicit claims (e.g., medication present in note) plus a manual spot-check sample (5% of failures) reviewed by a clinician. We'll include an 'assertion provenance' score when possible. Note: transcripts sometimes say K V cache, but we mean KV cache — apologies for the auto-transcript.

[04:50] Liam: About format checks: we're expecting a strict JSON schema for outputs used by downstream systems. Failures are not acceptable in production. Can Redwood enforce strict schema adherence and return structured error codes?

[05:05] Jordan: Yes — the runtime can validate output and return a structured error or fallback to a verified template. For the POC we'll log every schema failure and compute pass rate; target is 99%+ on golden prompts and 95%+ on the wider sample.

[05:24] Aisha: Scoring approach — how granular will the metrics be? We want per-field accuracy on structured outputs, hallucination per 100 responses, and an overall quality score to decide pass/fail.

[05:36] Maya: We'll compute per-field exact match / F1, an aggregate quality score weighted by business impact (e.g., diagnosis fields 40%, meds 30%, free-text summary 30%). Hallucination rate is reported separately. Also track latency and cost per 1k tokens.

[05:58] Jordan: For benchmarks we recommend baseline runs on two model configurations: 1) open LLM quantized on dedicated infra (fast, lower-cost) and 2) a higher-fidelity non-quantized variant to compare hallucination/accuracy tradeoffs. We'll include a fallback policy in the config.

[06:20] Liam: Can we run an A/B test during the POC? Like 10% to higher-fidelity model and 90% to cheaper config to see production tradeoffs.

[06:30] Maya: Absolutely — we'll include canary routing and collect metrics by route. We'll also instrument token-level cost and per-route latency.

[06:40] Sara: On security: we need audit logs, SSO/SAML integration, and data deletion process after the POC. Also want to understand encryption at rest and key management.

[06:54] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 summary and our KMS integration notes. For the POC we can use customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed keys with strict retention policies. Data deletion and audit logs are standard — we'll provide runbook.

[07:10] Aisha: Timeline check — we want pilot externally visible by mid-January. Can we make that?

[07:18] Jordan: Proposed timeline: Week 1 (this week): data contract and secure transfer; Week 2: baseline runs and golden prompt set finalized; Week 3: regression harness and initial eval; Week 4: iterate and produce pilot report. So yes, mid-January is feasible if data arrives on schedule.

[07:38] Liam: We'll aim to upload de-identified notes by 2026-12-10. That gives you time to run initial baselines.

[07:46] Maya: Great. For the eval config we'll include:
- Golden set size: 150 prompts (50 customer-provided + 100 Redwood variants)
- Metrics: per-field F1, hallucination per 100 responses, format pass rate, P95 latency, cost/1k tokens
- Pass criteria: aggregate quality score >=0.85 and hallucination <1% on golden set, format pass rate >=99%

[08:10] Aisha: That matches our ask.

[08:18] Jordan: Any blockers on data de-id or legal before you can share samples?

[08:24] Sara: Legal wants a short DPA addendum and confirmation of KMS options. We'll review the SOC2 summary once you send.

[08:34] Jordan: Understood — I'll send the SOC2 + DPA template and a quick checklist by Monday.

[08:42] Maya: I'll drop the benchmark repo link and starter prompts. For ocassion of transcription it sometimes garbles numbers — e.g., 'one twenty RPS' may show as 120R P S in transcript, please refer to the notes.

[08:56] Liam: Quick question on regression thresholds — the 2% degradation threshold, is that absolute or relative?

[09:02] Maya: Relative degradation on the primary metric. If you prefer absolute thresholds we can adapt.

[09:12] Aisha: We'll stick with relative for now.

[09:18] Jordan: Recap and next steps: Jordan to send security pack + SOC2 summary and DPA by 2026-12-06; Maya to share benchmark harness and starter golden prompts by 2026-12-07; CityHealth to upload 2 weeks de-id notes by 2026-12-10; follow-up to review initial results 2026-12-17.

[09:40] Sara: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[09:44] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up in email and get the files out.

[09:50] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript auto-caption had typical errors (KV -> K V, quantization -> quantizashion) and occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 1 instead of Jordan). The core action items and agreed metrics are above.
